subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. Turn “I am tired,” she said into She said she was tired, then report orders and questions.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। “I am tired,” she said-কে বানাও She said she was tired, তারপর আদেশ আর প্রশ্নও বলো।

hint.en: The tense moves one step back
No question mark, normal word order

rule.en: When the reporting verb is present (says), keep the tense. Just change the pronouns. “that” is optional.
rule.bn: Reporting verb present (says) হলে tense একই থাকে, শুধু pronoun বদলাও। “that” না দিলেও চলে।

recap.example: Rina says, “I love mangoes.” → Rina says she loves mangoes.

questions.prompt: Tom says, “I am busy.” → Tom says ___ busy.

options.why: Tom is talking about himself, so I becomes he.
says is present, so the tense doesn’t change.
he goes with is, not am.

questions.explanation: says: change the pronoun, keep the tense.

questions.prompt: Rafi says, “My phone is broken.” → Rafi says ___ phone is broken.

options.why: In reported speech, Rafi’s “my” becomes his.
Rafi is a boy, so use his.
The phone belongs to Rafi, not to the listener.

questions.prompt: Nila says, “I live in Sylhet.” Report it.

options.text: Nila says she lives in Sylhet.
Nila says she lived in Sylhet.
options.why: says is present, so keep the present: lives.

options.text: Nila says I live in Sylhet.
options.why: I must become she.

options.text: Nila says she live in Sylhet.
options.why: With she, add -s: lives.

questions.explanation: says + the same tense + a changed pronoun.

rule.en: When the reporting verb is past (said), move the tense one step back: am/is → was, are → were, present → past, past → had + V3.
rule.bn: Reporting verb past (said) হলে tense এক ধাপ পেছায়: am/is → was, are → were, present → past, past → had + V3।

recap.example: “I am tired.” → He said he was tired.

questions.prompt: She said, “I am cooking.” → She said she ___ cooking.

options.why: said is past, so is moves back to was.
am changes to was, and she doesn’t go with am.
The step back from am is was.

questions.prompt: He said, “I live in Khulna.” → He said he ___ in Khulna.

options.why: said is past, so the present moves back to the past.
That is two steps back. live → lived is one step.
The verb needs a tense: lived.

questions.prompt: Sara said, “I lost my keys.” Report it.

options.text: Sara said she had lost my keys.
options.why: my must become her.

options.text: Sara said she has lost her keys.
options.why: Use had, not has, after said.

options.text: Sara said she had lost her keys.
Sara said she had lose her keys.
options.why: After had, use V3: lost.

questions.explanation: past → had + V3, and my → her.

rule.en: Modals move back too: will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to.
rule.bn: Modal-ও এক ধাপ পেছায়: will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to।

recap.example: “I will help.” → She said she would help.

questions.prompt: He said, “I can drive.” → He said he ___ drive.

options.why: After said, can moves back to could.
would comes from will, not can.
No “to” after could.

questions.prompt: They said, “We will call you.” → They said they ___ call me.

options.why: After said, will moves back to would.
could comes from can, not will.
will changes to would.

questions.prompt: Mum said, “You must eat.” Report it.

options.text: Mum said I must to eat.
options.why: No “to” after must.

options.text: Mum said I had to ate.
options.why: After had to, use the base verb: eat.

options.text: Mum said I have to eat.
options.why: After said, use had to.

options.text: Mum said I had to eat.

questions.explanation: must → had to, and you → I.

rule.en: When you report later, change time and place words: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there, this → that.
rule.bn: পরে বললে সময় ও স্থানের শব্দ বদলাও: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there, this → that।

recap.example: “I’ll come tomorrow.” → She said she would come the next day.

questions.prompt: Last week, Rahim said, “I’ll come tomorrow.” → Rahim said he would come ___.

options.why: That “tomorrow” has already passed, so say the next day.
yesterday points the wrong way in time.
the day before replaces yesterday, not tomorrow.

questions.prompt: He said, “I met her yesterday.” → He said he had met her ___.

options.why: Change yesterday when you report it later.
the next day replaces tomorrow.
that day replaces today.

questions.explanation: yesterday → the day before (or the previous day).

questions.prompt: Rina said, “I am leaving today.” Report it.

options.text: Rina said she was leaving today.
options.why: Change today to that day.

options.text: Rina said she is leaving that day.
options.why: After said, am moves back to was.

options.text: Rina said I was leaving that day.
options.why: I must become she.

options.text: Rina said she was leaving that day.

questions.explanation: am → was, and today → that day.

rule.en: Use say + (that) … and tell + person + (that) …. Never say “said me”.
rule.bn: say + (that) …, আর tell + person + (that) …। কখনো “said me” বলবে না।

recap.example: She said hello. · She told me a story.

questions.prompt: He ___ me the truth.

options.why: say isn’t followed by a person. Use told me.
spoke doesn’t take a person and a thing like this.
talked needs to, and it still can’t take “the truth” like this.

questions.explanation: tell + person + thing: told me the truth.

questions.prompt: What did the doctor ___?

options.why: tell needs a person after it: tell you.
After did, use the base verb.
After did, use the base verb: say.

questions.explanation: No person after the verb → say.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: He said me that he was ill.
options.why: Never say “said me”. Use told me.

options.text: He told me that he was ill.
He told that he was ill.
options.why: tell needs a person: told me.

options.text: He told to me that he was ill.
options.why: No “to” after tell: told me.

cards.badge: told me to … · asked me not to …

rule.en: Report orders and requests with tell or ask + person + to + verb. For a negative, use not to + verb.
rule.bn: আদেশ বা অনুরোধ বলতে tell বা ask + person + to + verb। না-বোধক হলে not to + verb।

recap.example: “Sit down.” → He told me to sit down.

questions.prompt: “Don’t be late.” → She told us ___ late.

options.why: In reported orders, don’t becomes not to.
This is missing be. Say not to be.
We need to: not to be.

questions.prompt: “Please help me.” → He asked me ___ him.

options.why: After ask + person, use to + verb.
Use to + verb, not -ing.
For requests, use to + verb.

questions.prompt: The teacher said, “Open your books.” Report it.

options.text: The teacher told us open our books.
options.why: Add to: to open.

options.text: The teacher said us to open our books.
options.why: Never say “said us”. Use told us.

options.text: The teacher told us to open our books.
The teacher told us to open your books.
options.why: your becomes our.

rule.en: Report yes/no questions with ask + if (or whether). Use normal word order: subject + verb. No do/does/did and no question mark.
rule.bn: Yes/no প্রশ্ন বলতে ask + if (বা whether)। সাধারণ শব্দক্রম: subject + verb। do/does/did আর প্রশ্নবোধক চিহ্ন বসবে না।

recap.example: “Are you ready?” → She asked if I was ready.

questions.prompt: “Do you like tea?” → He asked me ___.

options.why: Reported questions don’t use question order or do.
Drop did and use normal order: I liked.
No question mark in reported questions.

questions.explanation: ask + if + subject + verb (one step back).

questions.prompt: “Is it raining?” → She asked ___ it was raining.

options.why: Questions are reported with if or whether, not that.
This is a yes/no question, so use if.
Don’t repeat the question word. Use if.

questions.prompt: “Can you swim?” he asked me. Report it.

options.text: He asked me if I could swim.
He asked me can I swim.
options.why: Use if and normal order: if I could swim.

options.text: He asked me if could I swim.
options.why: Use normal order after if: I could.

options.text: He asked me if I could swim?
options.why: No question mark in reported questions.

rule.en: Keep the wh- word, then use normal word order: subject + verb. No do/does/did and no question mark.
rule.bn: Wh- শব্দটি রাখো, তারপর সাধারণ শব্দক্রম: subject + verb। do/does/did আর প্রশ্নবোধক চিহ্ন বসবে না।

recap.example: “Where do you live?” → He asked where I lived.

questions.prompt: “What time is it?” → She asked ___.

options.why: Use normal order and move back: it was.
After the wh- word, put the subject first: it was.
Keep the wh- word at the front. Don’t use if.

questions.prompt: “Why are you crying?” → Mum asked me why I ___ crying.

options.why: After asked, am moves back to was.
With I, use was.
I goes with am or was, never is.

questions.prompt: “Where did you buy it?” she asked me. Report it.

options.text: She asked me where did I buy it.
options.why: No did, and use normal order.

options.text: She asked me where I had buy it.
options.why: After had, use V3: bought.

options.text: She asked me if where I had bought it.
options.why: Don’t use if with a wh- word.

options.text: She asked me where I had bought it.
